07abc1cc-5794-51a6-bad4-40565eae52be.title: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

e-4697.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
e-4697.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071933/assets/67d01790cfbda1f20a23c9e22a64714156485851ce56b2f73e9873db6ef4bed8.png)

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
e-4697.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -8 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071933/assets/da9c44be043ad3a15808a9e0dd77636697170047e61b73a0d591bc3581d992fb.png)

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=1$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+2(1)=0 
	\quad\Rightarrow\quad
	x=-2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-2$ and $y=1.$ Or, in vector form, $\left<  -2,1 \right>.$

e-4698.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
e-4698.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071933/assets/a80ecf94bbd4f0ea4b7a860e340039ca80bc5ccd0d2a19503cb9dcc571558976.png)
Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
e-4698.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071933/assets/ab29f353f00454b6e8eeb490336e2b33d0b2cf6cd47f4d24ac6c8a8f042af628.png)

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 1 & -6 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 0 & -1 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071933/assets/ee5b759f55931cf4935a0763f22c9eb5deedb04f3e247c295aa2a1da09b121b4.png)

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-10$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-5(-10)=-5 
	\quad\Rightarrow\quad
	x=-55.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-55$ and $y=-10.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -55,-10 \rangle.$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

b
M∼[1−3−920112], x=−3 and y=12
c
M∼[1−2−501172], x=42 and y=152

decision.explanation: Divide row 1 by 2 to obtain [1, −3, −9/2]. Subtract row 1 from row 2 to obtain [0, 1, 1/2]. Thus y = 1/2, and back substitution gives x − 3(1/2) = −9/2, so x = −3. This matches option b.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & -9 \\ 1 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & -9 \\ 1 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -\frac{9}{2} \\ 1 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -\frac{9}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y=-\frac{9}{2} \\  & y=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=\frac{1}{2}$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-3(\frac{1}{2})=-\frac{9}{2}\,⇒\,x=-\frac{9}{2}+\frac{3}{2}=-3.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-3$ and $y=\frac{1}{2}.$

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & -9 \\ 1 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & -9 \\ 1 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -\frac{9}{2} \\ 1 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -\frac{9}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y=-\frac{9}{2} \\  & y=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=\frac{1}{2}$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-3(\frac{1}{2})=-\frac{9}{2}\,⇒\,x=-\frac{9}{2}+\frac{3}{2}=-3.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-3$ and $y=\frac{1}{2}.$

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[118−1−23]. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce M to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.

a
M∼[1180111], x=10 and y=11
b
M∼[11801−16], x=17 and y=−16
c
M∼[11801−11], x=19 and y=−11
d
M∼[1180114], x=13 and y=14
e
M∼[1180113], x=11 and y=13
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R₂ ← R₂ + R₁ to get [0, −1, 11], then R₂ ← −R₂ to get [0, 1, −11]. Thus y = −11, and x + y = 8 gives x = 19. Option c matches both the row echelon form and the solution.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-1\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y=8 \\  & y=-11,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-11$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(-11)=8\,⇒\,x=8+11=19.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=19$ and $y=-11.$

EXPLANATION

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M∼[118−1−23]R2:=R2+1⋅R1∼[1180−111]R2:=−1⋅R2∼[11801−11].

The system is now
{x+y=8y=−11, and we can apply back substitution. The final equation y=−11 tells us the value of y. Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-1\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y=8 \\  & y=-11,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-11$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(-11)=8\,⇒\,x=8+11=19.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=19$ and $y=-11.$

M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 2 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}].

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[17−22100]. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce M to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.

a
M∼[17−101−2], x=12 and y=−2
b
M∼[17−1011], x=15 and y=1
c
M∼[17−201−1], x=13 and y=−1
d
M∼[17−1012], x=12 and y=2
e
M∼[17−201−1], x=5 and y=−1
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R₂ ← R₂ − 2R₁ to obtain [0, −4, 4], then divide row 2 by −4 to obtain [0, 1, −1]. Thus y = −1, and x + 7(−1) = −2 gives x = 5. Option e satisfies the entire request.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 2 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 2 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+7y=-2 \\  & y=-1,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-1$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+7(-1)=-2\,⇒\,x=-2+7=5.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=5$ and $y=-1.$

Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M∼[17−22100]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[17−20−44]R2:=−14R2∼[17−201−1].

The system is now
{x+7y=−2y=−1, and we can apply back substitution. The final equation y=−1 tells us the value of y. Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

Therefore, the solution is x=5 and y=−1.

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 2 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 2 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+7y=-2 \\  & y=-1,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-1$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+7(-1)=-2\,⇒\,x=-2+7=5.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=5$ and $y=-1.$

before.html:
Question 5
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[−121568]. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce M to row echelon form.

a
M∼[1−2−1011516]
b
M∼[1−2−1011116]
c
M∼[1−2−1011716]
d
M∼[1−2−1011316]
e
M∼[1−2−101916]
Submit

decision.explanation: Negate row 1 to obtain [1, −2, −1]. Then R₂ ← R₂ − 5R₁ gives [0, 16, 13]. Dividing row 2 by 16 gives [0, 1, 13/16], which matches option d.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 5 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-5\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 16 & 13\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{16}\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{13}{16}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 5 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-5\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 16 & 13\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{16}\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{13}{16}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 6
?

Consider the system of linear equations {2x−4y=64x−7y=10. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
M∼[1−2301−1], x=1 and y=−1
b
M∼[1−2301−4], x=−5 and y=−4
c
M∼[1−2301−2], x=−1 and y=−2
d
M∼[1−23014], x=11 and y=4
e
M∼[1−23012], x=7 and y=2
Submit

decision.explanation: Divide row 1 by 2 to obtain [1, −2, 3]. Then R₂ ← R₂ − 4R₁ gives [0, 1, −2]. Thus y = −2, and x − 2(−2) = 3 gives x = −1. This matches option c.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x-4y=6 \\  & 4x-7y=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 6 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 6 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y=3 \\  & y=-2,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-2$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(-2)=3\,⇒\,x=-1.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-1$ and $y=-2.$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x-4y=6 \\  & 4x-7y=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 6 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 6 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y=3 \\  & y=-2,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-2$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(-2)=3\,⇒\,x=-1.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-1$ and $y=-2.$

decision.explanation: Divide row 1 by 3 to obtain [1, 8/3, 22/3]. Then R₂ ← R₂ − 7R₁ gives [0, −71/3, −142/3]. Multiplying row 2 by −3/71 gives [0, 1, 2], matching option d.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x+8y=22 \\  & 7x-5y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 & 22 \\ 7 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 & 22 \\ 7 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{8}{3} & \frac{22}{3} \\ 7 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{8}{3} & \frac{22}{3} \\ 0 & -\frac{71}{3} & -\frac{142}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{3}{71}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{8}{3} & \frac{22}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x+8y=22 \\  & 7x-5y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 & 22 \\ 7 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 & 22 \\ 7 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{8}{3} & \frac{22}{3} \\ 7 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{8}{3} & \frac{22}{3} \\ 0 & -\frac{71}{3} & -\frac{142}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{3}{71}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{8}{3} & \frac{22}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 8
?

Consider the system of linear equations {3x−2y=42x−y=2. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form.

a
M∼[1−234301−2]
b
M∼[1−234301−32]
c
M∼[1−234301−3]
d
M∼[1−2343012]
e
M∼[1−23430132]
Submit

decision.explanation: Divide row 1 by 3 to obtain [1, −2/3, 4/3]. Then R₂ ← R₂ − 2R₁ gives [0, 1/3, −2/3]. Multiplying row 2 by 3 gives [0, 1, −2], matching option a.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x-2y=4 \\  & 2x-y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x-2y=4 \\  & 2x-y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 9
?

Consider the system of linear equations {2x+7y=−57x+11y=−4. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form.

a
M∼[172−5201−3]
b
M∼[172−5201−1]
c
M∼[17−501−2]
d
M∼[17−5010]
e
M∼[172−52011]
Submit

decision.explanation: Divide row 1 by 2 to obtain [1, 7/2, −5/2]. Then R₂ ← R₂ − 7R₁ gives [0, −27/2, 27/2]. Multiplying row 2 by −2/27 gives [0, 1, −1], matching option b.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x+7y=-5 \\  & 7x+11y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & -5 \\ 7 & 11 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & -5 \\ 7 & 11 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 7 & 11 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & -\frac{27}{2} & \frac{27}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{2}{27}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x+7y=-5 \\  & 7x+11y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & -5 \\ 7 & 11 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & -5 \\ 7 & 11 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 7 & 11 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & -\frac{27}{2} & \frac{27}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{2}{27}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Consider the system of linear equations {x+13y=113x+15y=9. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
M∼[11311010], x=11 and y=0
b
M∼[11311016], x=9 and y=6
c
M∼[1131101−3], x=12 and y=−3
d
M∼[113110130], x=1 and y=30
e
M∼[11311013], x=10 and y=3
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R₂ ← R₂ − 3R₁ to obtain [0, −4/5, −24]. Multiply row 2 by −5/4 to obtain [0, 1, 30]. Thus y = 30, and x + 30/3 = 11 gives x = 1. This matches option d.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+\frac{1}{3}y=11 \\  & 3x+\frac{1}{5}y=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 3 & \frac{1}{5} & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 3 & \frac{1}{5} & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 0 & -\frac{4}{5} & -24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{5}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 30\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+\frac{1}{3}y=11 \\  & y=30,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=30$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+\frac{1}{3}(30)=11\,⇒\,x=11-10=1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=1$ and $y=30.$

a
M∼[11311010], x=11 and y=0
b
M∼[11311016], x=9 and y=6
c
M∼[1131101−3], x=12 and y=−3
d
M∼[113110130], x=1 and y=30
e
M∼[11311013], x=10 and y=3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[113113159]. Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M∼[113113159]R2:=R2−3R1∼[113110−45−24]R2:=−54R2∼[113110130].

The system is now {x+13y=11y=30, and we can apply back substitution. The final equation y=30 tells us the value of y. Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

x+13(30)=11⇒x=11−10=1.

Therefore, the solution is x=1 and y=30.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+\frac{1}{3}y=11 \\  & 3x+\frac{1}{5}y=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 3 & \frac{1}{5} & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 3 & \frac{1}{5} & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 0 & -\frac{4}{5} & -24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{5}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 30\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+\frac{1}{3}y=11 \\  & y=30,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=30$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+\frac{1}{3}(30)=11\,⇒\,x=11-10=1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=1$ and $y=30.$
